saints.name: St. Rupert
saints.title: Bishop, Apostle of Bavaria
saints.shortBlurb: The missionary bishop who evangelized Bavaria and Austria and gave Salzburg its name and its Church…
biography: A Frankish bishop of Worms, Rupert was driven from that city by its still largely pagan people toward the end of the seventh century. Theodo, duke of Bavaria, then called him to Regensburg to preach the faith among the Bavarian tribes, and Rupert baptized the duke and many of his people.

He preached down the Danube as far as Lorch, the Roman Lauriacum, then made his seat in the ruined town of Juvavum, which he rebuilt and which came to be called Salzburg. There he restored the monastery of St. Peter, laid the foundations of the cathedral, and founded the nunnery of Nonnberg, where his niece Erentrude was first abbess.

From Duke Theodo he received estates at Reichenhall, where he fostered the saltworks that gave the city its name and him his emblem of a salt barrel. He died about 710; in 774 his successor Vergilius translated his relics to Salzburg Cathedral. He is honoured as apostle of the Bavarians and patron of Salzburg, the church he founded.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Church of Salzburg and evangelizing Bavaria.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 27 March
